Weekly Markets Monitor - Out of the ordinary

Highlights Geopolitical tensions and energy markets remained in focus last week, while investors also watched US data for clues on the Fed's policy path. A weaker-than-expected jobs report and stable PCE inflation reduced expectations of near-term rate hikes. Elsewhere, inflation accelerated in the Eurozone and Tokyo, China announced fresh growth-support measures and the Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates.  Major global equity markets ended the week mixed, while bond yields and the US dollar rose, and oil prices eased.  September was a highly unusual month. Gold in US$/oz fell by more than 8% despite more than 70t of global gold ETF inflows. The decline ranks in the 93rd percentile of monthly price falls, while the increase in ETF holdings ranks in the 77th percentile of monthly inflows1. We have not previously observed a month combining moves of this magnitude (C.O.T.W). The episode highlights diverging investor behaviour. While ETFs attracted more than 70t of inflows, COMEX Managed Money positions fell by 84t equivalents and the total Spreading (often associated with calendar spreads between futures maturities) category declined by 156t equivalents, helping to explain how gold prices weakened despite strong ETF demand.
